items.title: configure auto branch on git commit
items.body:
### Issue

I tested Aider for the first time yesterday. I simply asked a question about my repository to see what the model thought about an idea I had. To my great surprise, not only did it suggest a set of changes, it actually went ahead and committed those changes to the repository without asking me first. I then asked if it could commit all changes to a feature branch: it did create a feature branch, but the main branch was already dirtied, and I had to manually revert all changes.

There should at least be a configuration switch that will force to create a new branch before committing any changes, if the current branch is not a branch that was created by aider.

### Version and model info

Aider v0.86.1

items.title: Benchmark scores an exercise as solved based on a test command exit code that the model's own files control
items.body:
# Benchmark scores an exercise as solved based on a test command exit code that the model's own files control

Affected: Aider-AI/aider@5dc9490

## Summary

`run_unit_tests` decides whether an exercise was solved solely from the exit
code of a test command executed with `cwd=testdir`
(benchmark/benchmark.py:1027-1038). The testdir is the model-writable working
tree, and the benchmark harness auto-approves creation of new files (and
edits to existing files that were not added to the chat), so a response can
plant a file that forces the exit code to 0. A four line `conftest.py` makes
pytest exit 0 while every test fails, and the exercise is recorded with
`tests_outcomes: [true]` (benchmark/benchmark.py:889-893) and counts toward
`pass_rate_1`/`pass_rate_2` on the leaderboard.

The same primitive reaches the other languages because their runner config
files live in the exercise directory: `package.json` for JavaScript
(benchmark/npm-test.sh:12 runs `npm run test`), `CMakeLists.txt` for C++,
`build.gradle` for Java, `Cargo.toml` for Rust. Test files themselves are
restored from the pristine copy before each attempt
(benchmark/benchmark.py:1007-1014), but none of these runner config files
are.

## Why the harness auto-approves the payload

- The benchmark creates `InputOutput(pretty=False, yes=True, ...)`
  (benchmark/benchmark.py:786-790).
- With `yes is True`, `confirm_ask` returns "y" without asking
  (aider/io.py:866-867).
- `allowed_to_edit` asks "Create new file?" for a path that does not exist
  (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2206-2224) and "Allow edits to file that has
  not been added to the chat?" for one that does
  (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2226-2240). Both are auto-approved.

The docker warning (benchmark/benchmark.py:252-254) is about the safety of
running unvetted code on the host. It does not cover this: the score itself
is what is compromised, and a gamed run is indistinguishable from an honest
one in the results yaml and on the leaderboard, which accepts
community-submitted results (benchmark/README.md,
aider/website/docs/leaderboards/contrib.md).

## Reproduction

The PoC vendors `run_unit_tests` and the try-loop decision verbatim from
benchmark/benchmark.py (lines 981-1049 and 889-893) and runs them on a
fabricated python exercise (leap year) whose solution file is deliberately
wrong in both arms. The only difference between the arms is a
model-creatable `conftest.py`.

```
python3 -m pip install --target /tmp/aider-poc-deps pytest
R8E2_DEPS=/tmp/aider-poc-deps python3 poc_f1_grader_exit_code.py f1-evidence.json
```

(`R8E2_DEPS` is only used to put a working `pytest` on PATH, mirroring the
benchmark container. Any environment with `pytest` importable works.)

Observed (evidence file, deterministic across runs):

- control arm: wrong implementation, no conftest: pytest exit code 1,
  failure output returned, benchmark records outcome `False`
- conftest arm: the identical wrong implementation plus this `conftest.py`:

  ```
  def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
      if exitstatus != 0:
          session.exitstatus = 0
  ```

  pytest exit code 0, `run_unit_tests` returns None, benchmark records
  outcome `True`, i.e. solved. The chat history still contains the FAILED
  test lines while the exercise is scored solved.

The PoC asserts the implementation file is byte-identical between the arms,
so the flip is attributable to the exit-code channel alone.

## Impact

- Any model that emits a `conftest.py` (or rewrites `package.json`,
  `CMakeLists.txt`, `build.gradle`) converts every failing exercise of that
  language into a solved one. On the 225 exercise polyglot set this is a
  path to an arbitrary leaderboard score without solving any task.
- The python arm and the approval chain are executed/proved at the pin; the
  JavaScript/C++/Java/Rust arms follow from the same approval chain plus the
  runner config files being model-editable and not restored, but were not
  executed here.
- It also silently invalidates cross-model comparisons: a run is recorded
  with the same `model`, `edit_format` and cost fields as an honest one.

## Suggestions

- Restore the whole exercise directory from the pristine copy before each
  test attempt, except the specific solution files the model was given, so
  no model-created artifact can influence the test run.
- Or run the tests in a scratch copy containing only the restored test files
  plus the solution files, with an explicit pytest config
  (`-c`, `-p no:cacheprovider`, fixed `--rootdir`) so no in-tree conftest or
  ini file is picked up.
- Additionally parse the test output for the pass/fail summary instead of
  trusting the exit code alone, and treat a 0-exit run whose summary shows
  failures as a harness error rather than a solved exercise.

items.title: Add auto mode for automated task execution without confirmation
items.body:
## Description

This PR adds a new automation mode for aider that can perform tasks automatically without requiring confirmation for each step, with enhanced context-finding capabilities.

## Features

### Auto Mode
- Created a new `AutoCoder` class that inherits from `ContextCoder`
- Sets `yes_to_all = True` to bypass confirmations
- Sets `auto_accept_architect = True` to automatically accept architect changes
- Automatically adds files and applies changes
- Added a new command `/auto` to switch to this mode

### Enhanced Context Finding
- Added a new `get_enhanced_file_mentions` method that uses multiple strategies to identify relevant files
- Reduced the minimum identifier length from 5 to 3 characters to catch more potential matches
- Added detection of parent directory names and path components
- Added detection of import statements and package references
- Increased token allocation for the repository map by 50% to provide more context
- Added command-line options to control context finding behavior

## How to Use

Users can now use the auto mode in several ways:

1. Start aider with the auto mode:
   ```
   aider --chat-mode auto
   ```

2. Start aider with auto mode but disable enhanced context finding:
   ```
   aider --chat-mode auto --no-deep-context-search
   ```

3. Customize the minimum identifier length:
   ```
   aider --chat-mode auto --min-identifier-length 4
   ```

4. Switch to auto mode during a session:
   ```
   /chat-mode auto
   ```

5. Use the auto mode for a single command:
   ```
   /auto <your request>
   ```

In auto mode, aider will:
1. Automatically identify which files need to be edited using enhanced context finding
2. Add those files to the chat context
3. Make the necessary changes without asking for confirmation
4. Run linting and testing if configured

This mode is particularly useful for automating repetitive tasks or for users who want a more streamlined experience without the need to confirm each step.

## Issues Fixed

This PR also includes fixes for several issues that were encountered during testing:

### 1. TypeError in base_coder.py

The first issue was a TypeError in base_coder.py (line 181) where the `deep_context_search` parameter was being passed to the `Coder.__init__` method, but the method didn't accept this parameter:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
  File "__main__.py", line 7, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
             ^^^^^^
  File "main.py", line 959, in main
    coder = Coder.create(
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "base_coder.py", line 181, in create
    res = coder(main_model, io, **kwargs)
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: Coder.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'deep_context_search'
```

This was fixed by:
- Adding the `deep_context_search` and `min_identifier_length` parameters to the `Coder.__init__` method
- Storing these parameters as instance variables in the `Coder` class
- Adding a base implementation of the `get_enhanced_file_mentions` method to the `Coder` class

### 2. UnicodeDecodeError in JSON Loading

The second issue was a UnicodeDecodeError when loading JSON files with non-ASCII characters:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "utils.py", line 188, in <module>
    json_data = json.load(f)
                ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "__init__.py", line 293, in load
    return loads(fp.read(),
                 ^^^^^^^^^^
  File "cp1252.py", line 23, in decode
    return codecs.charmap_decode(input,self.errors,decoding_table)[0]
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x81 in position 1980: character maps to <undefined>
```

This was fixed by:
1. Adding a global JSON loading patch in `aider/llm.py` that handles UTF-8 encoding for all JSON files loaded by litellm
2. Updating file reading methods in `base_coder.py` to handle UnicodeDecodeError exceptions:
   - `get_abs_fnames_content`
   - `choose_fence`
   - `get_read_only_files_content`

These changes ensure that binary files (like MP3s, MP4s, and other non-text files) are gracefully handled and don't cause the application to crash with UnicodeDecodeError.

### 3. Token Limit Exceeded with Enhanced Context Finding

When using the enhanced context finding feature, there's a potential issue with exceeding token limits, especially in large codebases:

```
Tokens: 13k sent, 395 received. Cost: $0.04 message, $0.08 session.
Warning: it's best to only add files that need changes to the chat.
https://aider.chat/docs/troubleshooting/edit-errors.html
Automatically added files: [long list of files...]
Your estimated chat context of 1,530,131 tokens exceeds the 200,000 token limit for openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet!
To reduce the chat context:
- Use /drop to remove unneeded files from the chat
- Use /clear to clear the chat history
- Break your code into smaller files
It's probably safe to try and send the request, most providers won't charge if the context limit is exceeded.
litellm.BadRequestError: OpenrouterException - Message: This endpoint's maximum context length is 200000 tokens. However, you requested about 1606966 tokens (1542966 of text input, 64000 in the output). 
Please reduce the length of either one, or use the "middle-out" transform to compress your prompt automatically., Metadata: {'provider_name': None}, User ID:
```

This is a known limitation when using enhanced context finding in large codebases. Users should be aware that they may need to:
1. Use `/drop` to remove unneeded files from the chat
2. Use `/clear` to clear the chat history
3. Use `--no-deep-context-search` to disable enhanced context finding in very large codebases
4. Increase the `--min-identifier-length` parameter to reduce the number of matches
